Round 4 refused six dsbb.imf.org edges and three more on the DQAF Monetary PDF on the edition rule: the SDDS and SDDS Plus 'Internationally Accepted Statistical Methodologies' tables and the DQAF for Monetary Statistics all name the 2004 CPI Manual, the 2000 MFSM and the 2008 MFS Compilation Guide by title and year, while the corpus carried only their successors (cpi-manual, the 2020 edition; imf-mfsmcg-2016, the 2016 merger of the other two). This slice mints the three superseded editions the documents actually cite, wires the nine edges, and records the three supersedes relations that tie each old edition to the node that replaced it. Every quote below was verified character-for-character against the document on 2026-09-06: the two dsbb methodology pages from Thomas's own Chrome capture (dsbb.imf.org is an AngularJS shell; recipe in notes/imf-dsbb-2026-09-06.md), the DQAF PDF and the four elibrary book PDFs by plain browser-UA curl from the cloud sandbox (recipe in notes/imf-elibrary-2026-09-06.md). One refusal from the same pass produced no node and stays recorded on its original entry in int-imf-dsbb-2026-09-06.json rather than being copied here: the SDDS tables' 2009 draft International Recommendations for the Index of Industrial Production has no live address, and a document with no live address cannot be a node.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index Manual: Theory and Practice (2004)
reports.publisher: ILO, IMF, OECD, Eurostat, United Nations and the World Bank
reports.description: The 2004 edition of the internationally agreed manual of concepts, methods and practice for compiling a consumer price index, managed by the ILO and published jointly by six international organisations whose names appear on its title page. Superseded in 2020 by the Consumer Price Index Manual: Concepts and Methods (the corpus node cpi-manual), which describes itself as an update of this edition. Minted as its own node because the IMF's SDDS and SDDS Plus methodology tables cite this edition by title and year rather than the 2020 successor, and the corpus models editions as separate nodes.

reports.title: Monetary and Financial Statistics Manual (2000)
reports.description: The IMF's 2000 manual of concepts, definitions and classifications for monetary and financial statistics — the sectorisation of the financial corporations sector, the classification of financial assets, and the surveys of the central bank, other depository corporations and other financial corporations that the standard monetary statistics are built from. Superseded in 2016 by the Monetary and Financial Statistics Manual and Compilation Guide (the corpus node imf-mfsmcg-2016), which states in its first chapter that it combines and updates this Manual and the 2008 Compilation Guide. Minted as its own node because the SDDS, SDDS Plus and DQAF for Monetary Statistics all cite the 2000 edition by title and year.

reports.title: Monetary and Financial Statistics: Compilation Guide (2008)
reports.description: The IMF's 2008 companion to the 2000 Monetary and Financial Statistics Manual, written for national compilers: it takes the Manual's methodology and statistical frameworks down to the level of source data, account-by-account classification and the standardised report forms the IMF collects monetary data on. Superseded in 2016 by the Monetary and Financial Statistics Manual and Compilation Guide (imf-mfsmcg-2016), which merged it with the Manual. Cited by the SDDS and SDDS Plus methodology tables under its full title and by the DQAF for Monetary Statistics as the 'MFS Compilation Guide', which is the alias below.

Only plain pdftotext reading order rejoins them. The Preface is single-column and has no such break. via: direct read of the live host, cloud sandbox browser-UA curl, 2026-09-06; the whole-book PDF on this ISBN served all 372 pages today, correcting the front-matter-only reading taken earlier the same day.

_dropped.why: REFUSED 2026-09-06 (round 5, little thing 2), re-checked now that a 2004 node exists. The DQAF for the Consumer Price Index names 'the Consumer Price Index Manual (CPI Manual)' with no year and no edition anywhere in its Methodological Soundness section, so it names the family rather than an edition, and the edition rule treats a family reference as naming no edition (Report.title_aliases rule 1). This is a refusal on the citing document's own wording, not on the absence of a node, so minting cpi-manual-2004 does not change it. Re-open only if a DQAF revision dates the manual it assesses against.
